meta.title: CloverProof — Field-specific fertilizer decisions, with proof
meta.description: CloverProof turns your field and soil-test data into a fertilizer plan — what, how much, when and why — reviewed by an agronomist and recorded in a proof document. Vendor-neutral, software only.

hero.title: A clearer plan for every field.
hero.lead: CloverProof connects your soil tests, field history and crop goals into one fertilizer plan — what to apply, how much, when, and why — checked by an agronomist before it reaches you.
hero.note: Early-stage product. Pilot availability depends on location and fit.
hero.figureCaption: Every recommendation is tied to one field, one season and one set of inputs.
hero.imageAlt: Young winter wheat in long rows at sunrise, with clover leaves in the foreground

problem.title: The practical problem
problem.intro: Fertilizer decisions are often made from scattered records and general advice, with no trace of the reasoning.

items.title: Records live in different places.
items.body: Lab reports in email, spreader logs in a notebook, crop history in someone's memory. Nothing is joined up for the field in front of you.

items.title: Advice is generic — or tied to a product.
items.body: Blanket rates ignore the field. Advice from a supplier is shaped by what they sell. Neither shows its working.

items.title: No record of why.
items.body: When a season goes well or badly, there is nothing to look back on: which inputs were used, which assumptions were made, who signed off.

how.title: How it works
how.intro: Four steps, the same every time. Nothing reaches you without a person checking it.

steps.title: Farm data
steps.body: Your field, crop, target yield and previous crop. A lab soil test if you have one — with its method, depth and date.

steps.title: Engine
steps.body: A transparent calculation runs against a versioned set of regional rules. Every number gets a written reason and a confidence level.

steps.title: Agronomist review
steps.body: An agronomist approves, adjusts or rejects the plan. Any change is saved as a new version with the reason — the original is never overwritten.

steps.title: Proof document
steps.body: You receive a plan document: what, how much, when and why, with the reviewer, the versions used and a digital fingerprint.

proof.title: What a proof document shows
proof.intro: A sample layout. Values are left blank on purpose — real values only appear once an agronomist has reviewed your field.
whyLines: Crop need for the target yield, from the regional rule set.
Supply already in the soil, from the lab test.
proof.disclaimer: A proof document records what was recommended and why. It is not a certification and is not issued or endorsed by any third party.

items.title: Vendor-neutral
items.body: We don't sell fertilizer and we don't take commissions on it.

items.title: Software only
items.body: No sensors or hardware to buy. We work from your field information and lab results.

items.title: Confidence on every number
items.body: Each recommendation is marked high, medium or low confidence, with the reason.

items.title: No soil test, nitrogen only
items.body: Without a lab test we only advise on nitrogen, and recommend a test for phosphorus and potassium.

items.title: Every edit is versioned
items.body: Plans are never overwritten. Changes are saved as new versions with who changed what, and why.

items.a: No. CloverProof is independent of any supplier. The plan names nutrients and rates, not brands.

items.q: Do I need sensors or special equipment?
items.a: No. CloverProof is software only. We work from your field details and, where available, a laboratory soil test.

items.q: What if I don't have a soil test?
items.a: We can still advise on nitrogen, at medium confidence at most. For phosphorus and potassium we'll recommend getting a test first.
Every plan is reviewed by an agronomist before you see it. If they change a number, the reason is recorded.

items.q: What is the proof document for?
items.a: It's your record of what was recommended, on what inputs, and why. It is not a certification and no third party has endorsed it.
We're starting with a small number of farms. Availability depends on location, crop and fit — request a plan and we'll tell you honestly.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: How CloverProof collects, uses and protects the details you share when you request a pilot plan.

sections.p: When you request a pilot plan we collect the details you enter: name, email, country, approximate farm size, main crop and any notes.
Only to assess whether we can include your farm in the pilot and to contact you about it. We don't sell or share your details for marketing.
Your details are stored in our database provider with access limited to the CloverProof team.
Until the pilot selection is complete, or longer if you join the pilot. You can ask us to delete your details at any time.
You can ask to see, correct or delete your data, and withdraw consent at any time.

check.title: What could your plan cover?
check.intro: Answer four quick questions. Each answer fills a leaf. At the end you'll see what kind of plan we could build for this field — before you share anything.

questions.q: Do you have a lab soil test for this field?
Does the report show the extraction method and sampling depth?
questions.hint: For example Olsen, Bray-1 or Mehlich-3, and the depth in cm or inches.

questions.q: Do you know what grew on this field last season?
Do you have a realistic yield target for this season?

full.title: A full nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium plan
full.body: With a complete lab report we can plan all three nutrients, each with its own confidence level and reasons.

confirm.title: A full plan, once we confirm the lab method
confirm.body: You have a soil test. We'll ask for the report so we can read the extraction method and depth — then plan all three nutrients.

nOnly.title: A nitrogen plan — and a soil test for the rest
nOnly.body: Without a lab test we only advise on nitrogen, at medium confidence at most. For phosphorus and potassium we'll recommend a test first.

gaps.previousCrop: Last season's crop — it changes how much nitrogen the soil already supplies.
gaps.target: A yield target — the plan is built around it.
gaps.method: The lab's extraction method and sampling depth.
gaps.soilTest: A lab soil test for phosphorus and potassium.

check.noGaps: Nothing missing. This field is ready for a plan.
check.cta: Request a pilot plan for this field
check.disclaimer: This check only shows the scope of a plan. It gives no rates — those come after an agronomist reviews your data.
